analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md adds two rows at head lines 553-555, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION`, under the Memory and media budgets table. I reviewed both base excerpts (lines 354-687), which are surrounding context, against the supplied patch excerpt. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the tail of the second row is not visible. No source code, authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator protocol logic changes.

Security-relevant observations on the described behavior:
- T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and A-001: the second row says paged pools retain up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8) of free KV segments, uncommitted and uncharged, and reinstall them at admission instead of allocating, filling and fencing new ones. That could mean KV segment memory is reused across requests or consumers without being zeroed or fenced.
- The row says new segments are zero-fill-on-demand host pages, but the visible text is cut off. Whether reinstalled retained segments are scrubbed before reuse is not shown, so cross-request KV residue exposure (T-028) cannot be ruled in or out from this doc change.
- T-029 and T-010 (availability, memory pressure): retention is dropped on refused admission, memory pressure, a load gate and 30 s of idleness. Memory is described as uncharged but reclaimable, so DoS exposure looks bounded by the design as documented.
- Both controls are kill switches that default on and are forwarded to the launchd job. This widens runtime behavior but is not a new trust boundary.

The underlying source files (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, KVPoolReclaimer.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) were not supplied. I cannot verify that segment reuse preserves the zeroing/isolation invariants, so I flag that for the integration pass rather than raise a finding. The remaining question for that pass is whether retained, reinstalled KV segments are cleared before reuse; T-028 may need a note that segment retention is in scope. No concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied text.
